newsitem.title: UK: London banks in talks on loan trading market.
newsitem.headline: London banks in talks on loan trading market.

text.p: Plans to set up a standardised secondary market in bank loans are being discussed by a group of London-based banks, loan market sources confirmed on Friday.

Market sources confirmed a newspaper report that talks were going on but added that these had been underway for some time and that the banks were now closer to agreeing a more standardised structure for the market.
"This is a very logical next step forward in the development of this market," one loan market participant said, adding that further details should emerge during December.
The Evening Standard newspaper said the Bank of England (BoE) had been kept informed of the development of the market but added that it would not have a formal supervisory role.
"A group of banks has kept the Bank informed of their plans," a BoE official told Reuters.

There is already a secondary market in bank loans in the UK but a more active and liquid market would, among other things, enable banks to manage their loan portfolios more efficiently and free-up capital, sources said.
The discussions under way are aimed at standardising and simplifying the existing system and will include the borrowers whose loans are at the core of the market, one added.
Plans are not limited to loans to UK-listed companies and any scheme would also encompass European markets, some of which are already reasonably active.
Market sources confirmed that the seven banks involved at this stage are Barclays, HSBC, NatWest Markets, J.P. Morgan, SBC Warburg, Credit Suisse and Fuji Bank.
